warrant: The observable follows counter-streaming electron transport, nonlinear distribution evolution, conserved moments and self-consistent electrostatic growth; alpha (line 71) seeds the instability at 1e-6. A wrong DG transport flux, charge sign, current accumulation or field solve changes the nonlinear histories at order one; the mechanisms are under vlasov/zero/ and vlasov/apps/. The instability amplifies the two-ULP alpha change: 4.7e-8 on the x86 worker (2026-09-05), 1.35e-7 on the author's arm64, and the strict-IEEE altbuild (same source, gcc -O2, no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native) differs by 7.9e-8. The bound is atol=2e-5 with rtol=1e-11 (confirmed at review on 2026-09-04, an earlier round): about 250 times the larger floor, and the absolute term governs every graded value. The blind spot, counted in the nominal record: 110,560 of the 127,560 field-energy samples and 21,260 of the 63,780 moment values lie below 2e-5, the linear-growth stage, and are judged by the absolute term alone. A fault confined to that stage without shifting the later trajectory would pass; a wrong growth rate shifts the saturation time and with it the O(100) saturated history, which the bound catches.
